دَارِئٌ Coming from a place, or from a distant place, unexpectedly: (M, TA: but only the pls. of the word in this sense are there mentioned:) an enemy showing open hostility, or coming forth into the field to encounter another in battle: and a stranger: (T:) pl. دُرَأ=ءُ (T, M, TA) and دُرَّآءٌ. (M, TA.) People say, نَحْنُ فُقَرَآءُ دُرَأ=ءُ [We are poor men, come from a distant place, or strangers]. (T, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 1, last sentence. ―
-b2- [Hence,] metaphorically used by Ru-beh as meaning (tropical:) Swollen with anger. (M, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
